headline_marked: 200+ masked men [[raze Mirpur health centre]], DMP commissioner orders probe
headline: 200+ masked men raze Mirpur health centre, DMP commissioner orders probe
summary: The Radda MCH-FP Centre was vandalized and looted late at night; four people have been arrested as police investigate negligence in the attack.
details: Over 200 masked individuals armed with local weapons attacked, looted, and demolished the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1, Dhaka, during the late-night hours.
Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman questioned the role of law enforcement and the administration, calling the attack a deprivation of essential healthcare for local residents.
The DMP commissioner has ordered a probe into whether police negligence allowed the overnight demolition of the healthcare facility.
A three-member body has been formed to investigate the police's role in the attack, while four suspects have already been arrested and sent to jail.
Following the attack, a 'mysterious' signboard was reportedly placed at the site, further complicating the incident.
Looted materials from the vaccination center have been recovered by authorities.
The Democratic Rights Committee has described the incident as a 'terrorist attack' on people's right to live, while other leaders have questioned the state's authority in the city.
caption:
Over 200 masked men demolished a health centre in Mirpur overnight. Who was behind it?

Over 200 masked individuals armed with local weapons attacked, looted, and demolished the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1, Dhaka, during the late-night hours.

Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman questioned the role of law enforcement and the administration, calling the attack a deprivation of essential healthcare for local residents.

The DMP commissioner has ordered a probe into whether police negligence allowed the overnight demolition of the healthcare facility.

A three-member body has been formed to investigate the police's role in the attack, while four suspects have already been arrested and sent to jail.

Following the attack, a 'mysterious' signboard was reportedly placed at the site, further complicating the incident.

Looted materials from the vaccination center have been recovered by authorities.

The Democratic Rights Committee has described the incident as a 'terrorist attack' on people's right to live, while other leaders have questioned the state's authority in the city.

#Bangladesh #Dhaka #Mirpur #Healthcare #News #Justice

Source: Dhaka Tribune, The Daily Star, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, bdnews24.com

headline_marked: Police raid JaSaD office, detain [[nearly 300 people]] over alleged Awami League meeting
headline: Police raid JaSaD office, detain nearly 300 people over alleged Awami League meeting
summary: Authorities detained hundreds from the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) headquarters in Dhaka's Gulistan, citing information about a gathering of banned Awami League activists. Legal action is pending verification of their identities and activities.
details: Police have detained approximately 280 to 300 individuals following a raid on the Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal (JaSaD) headquarters in Dhaka's Gulistan area. The operation, which began Saturday afternoon, saw detainees transported to Paltan Police Station in handcuffs.

Authorities stated the raid was prompted by information suggesting that activists of the Awami League, a party banned from political activities, had convened at the JaSaD office for alleged sabotage or other unlawful purposes. Local students and members of the public reportedly assisted the police in the operation.

Motijheel Deputy Commissioner Mohammad Harun-or-Rashid confirmed the number of detainees and indicated that authorities were verifying the reasons for their gathering, their affiliations, and any activities undertaken. Reports of "Joy Bangla" slogans being heard at the location were also being investigated.

Among those detained was former Dhaka Union of Journalists President Abu Jafar Surya, who claimed he was performing professional duties at a JaSaD representatives’ meeting. He posted a handcuffed photo on Facebook, stating his detention.

JaSaD Office Secretary Sazzad Hossain, however, rejected the allegations of a secret Awami League meeting as false. He claimed that BNP and Jatiotabadi Jubo Dal activists had attacked their meeting, and that police removed them before detaining JaSaD members.

The detained individuals were initially taken to Paltan Police Station for security and to ascertain the facts of the incident. Police indicated that legal action would be pursued against those found involved, while others would be released after verification. They were also checking if any journalists or individuals from other professions were among the detainees.
